lessons.title: The workplace

sentences.english: What is your profession?
My position is manager.
My brother works as a doctor.
Our office is very nice.
The manager is on a business trip today.

sentences.target: У меня новый клиент и большой проект.
sentences.english: I have a new client and a big project.
sentences.translit: U menya novyy kliyent i bol'shoy proyekt.

fills.english: He works as a teacher at a school.

dialogue.scene: A new colleague asks about you.

lines.english: Hi! Are you the new employee?

lines.target: Да, я работаю в этой компании с понедельника.

lines.translit: Otlichno! A kakaya u tebya dolzhnost'?

lessons.tip: Work as a profession takes the instrumental: работать + врачом, программистом. Just add the -ом ending to the job.

sentences.english: I need a good reference.

fills.english: I want to quit on Friday.
What experience do you have?
They gave me a promotion.
I have a good education.

dialogue.scene: A friend checks your job hunt.

lines.english: So, how is the job hunt?

lines.target: Я отправил резюме в пять компаний.

lines.translit: Ya otpravil rezyume v pyat' kompaniy.

lines.english: And? Is there an interview?

lessons.tip: Result = perfect verb: уволиться (to quit, done) vs увольняться (the process). 'Я уволился' means it is finished.

items.english: to agree on, to get approved

sentences.translit: Vo vlozhenii moy otchyot i rezyume.

sentences.english: Please review my application.

Write 'Dear Sergey Ivanovich!'
And how do I end the letter?

lessons.tip: Formal letters run on chunks: Уважаемый + name ... С уважением. Learn the chunk whole, do not take it apart.

sentences.english: Happy New Year! Wishing you happiness!

lines.translit: Cherez minutu Novyy god! Nalit' tebe shampanskoye?

Do you want to make a toast?

lessons.tip: Congratulate with с + instrumental: С Новым годом! С Рождеством! С днём рождения! The holiday sits after с in the -ом/-ом form.

lessons.title: Food culture

sentences.target: На обед я люблю борщ со сметаной.

sentences.translit: Na obed ya lyublyu borshch so smetanoy.

sentences.english: In summer I like cold kvass.

lines.target: Садись за стол! Сегодня у нас борщ и пельмени.

lines.english: It smells so good!

replyOptions: Нет, я люблю квас с хлебом ночью.

lessons.tip: Many Russian dishes are plural words: пельмени, блины, щи, пирожки. Pair them with plural verbs: Блины готовы!

lessons.title: Customs

sentences.translit: My lyubim khodit' v banyu zimoy.

Thank you! May I take my shoes off?

lessons.title: Building arguments

items.english: in the end, as a result

sentences.target: Во-первых, это дорого. Во-вторых, это далеко.
sentences.english: Firstly, it is expensive. Secondly, it is far.
sentences.translit: Vo-pervykh, eto dorogo. Vo-vtorykh, eto daleko.

sentences.english: Besides, it is very noisy there.

sentences.target: С одной стороны, это хорошая работа.
sentences.english: On the one hand, it is a good job.
sentences.translit: S odnoy storony, eto khoroshaya rabota.

sentences.target: С другой стороны, у меня нет времени.
sentences.english: On the other hand, I have no time.
sentences.translit: S drugoy storony, u menya net vremeni.

sentences.english: I like fruit, for example apples.

sentences.target: Мы долго думали и в итоге остались дома.
sentences.english: We thought for a long time and in the end stayed home.
sentences.translit: My dolgo dumali i v itoge ostalis' doma.

fills.english: Firstly, I am tired.
I need a rest, that is, a holiday.
We worked a lot, so in the end the project is ready.

fills.after: , это дёшево, а с другой — далеко.
fills.english: On the one hand, it is cheap, and on the other, far.

dialogue.scene: Deciding where to go on holiday.

lines.target: Почему ты не хочешь ехать на море?
lines.english: Why don't you want to go to the sea?
lines.translit: Pochemu ty ne khochesh' yekhat' na more?

lines.english: Firstly, it is very expensive.
And secondly?

lessons.tip: Linkers carry the logic: во-первых, во-вторых, в-третьих lines up your points. Say them as a set and your argument sounds organised.

lessons.title: Agreeing

sentences.english: Yes, exactly like that!
Exactly! I think so too.
I absolutely agree with you.
You are right, this is an important question.

sentences.target: В этом есть смысл, давай попробуем.
sentences.english: That makes sense, let's try.
sentences.translit: V etom yest' smysl, davay poprobuyem.

sentences.english: Undoubtedly, it is logical and fair.

fills.english: You are right, I was wrong.
I agree with you.
This is very logical.
Of course, I will help you.

dialogue.scene: Deciding on a plan with a colleague.

lines.english: Let's meet tomorrow morning.
Fine, what time?
At nine. Does that work?

lessons.tip: Agree with a one-word punch: Именно! Точно! Безусловно! Short and strong is how real people agree.

lessons.title: Disagreeing

sentences.english: Not quite. It is a bit different.

sentences.target: Я не уверен, что это правда.
sentences.english: I am not sure that it is true.
sentences.translit: Ya ne uveren, shto eto pravda.

sentences.english: He is unlikely to come today.
I doubt that it is a good idea.

sentences.target: На самом деле я не люблю зиму.
sentences.english: Actually, I do not like winter.
sentences.translit: Na samom dele ya ne lyublyu zimu.

sentences.english: No, on the contrary, I really like it!

fills.english: He hardly knows.
I doubt that.
He is not evil, on the contrary, he is kind.
You are mistaken, that is not so.

dialogue.scene: A friendly disagreement about a film.

lines.english: This film is very boring, right?
Not quite. I liked it.
Really? And what did you like?

lessons.tip: Soften, then oppose: Не совсем так... Я не уверен, что... is polite. Save отнюдь and вы ошибаетесь for serious moments.

lessons.title: Participles lite

sentences.english: This is a book written in 1900.
The window is open and the door is closed.
Pushkin is a famous Russian poet.
My favourite city is Petersburg.
A reading person always knows a lot.
Don't wake the sleeping child.

lessons.tip: -щий = who does it (говорящий, читающий); -нный/-тый = done to it (написанный, открытый). Nothing new to learn, they decline like normal adjectives.

lessons.title: Facts & claims

sentences.english: This is a fact, not an opinion.
I have a good argument.
What is the cause of this problem?

sentences.target: Я хочу доказать, что это правда.

sentences.target: Мы обсуждаем план, а не спорим.
sentences.english: We are discussing a plan, not arguing.
sentences.translit: My obsuzhdayem plan, a ne sporim.

sentences.target: Я признаю, что был не прав.
sentences.english: I admit that I was wrong.

dialogue.scene: A debate between colleagues.

lines.target: Ты не прав, и у меня есть довод.

lines.english: Okay, I am listening.

lines.english: Here is a fact: the client wants a different deadline.
lines.translit: Vot fakt: kliyent khochet drugoy srok.

lessons.tip: Reasoning verbs come in pairs: доказывать/доказать, убеждать/убедить. Learn the finished one (доказать, убедить) for 'I managed to'.

lessons.tip: Animals carry stereotypes, often like English (busy as a bee = белка в колесе). When it does not match, just remember the picture.

lessons.title: Proverbs

items.english: repetition is the mother of learning
slow and steady wins the race

sentences.target: Я встал ни свет ни заря.
sentences.english: I got up at the crack of dawn.
sentences.translit: Ya vstal ni svet ni zarya.

sentences.target: В один прекрасный день я уеду в Россию.
sentences.english: One fine day I will go to Russia.
sentences.translit: V odin prekrasnyy den' ya uyedu v Rossiyu.

sentences.english: Time is money, let's hurry up.

sentences.target: Не спеши: семь раз отмерь, один отрежь.
sentences.english: Don't hurry: measure twice, cut once.
sentences.translit: Ne speshi: sem' raz otmer', odin otrezh'.

sentences.target: Ты пришёл поздно, но лучше поздно, чем никогда!
sentences.english: You came late, but better late than never!
sentences.translit: Ty prishyol pozdno, no luchshe pozdno, chem nikogda!

sentences.target: Мир тесен: я встретил друга в Москве.
sentences.english: It's a small world: I met a friend in Moscow.
sentences.translit: Mir tesen: ya vstretil druga v Moskve.

fills.english: Repetition is the mother of learning.
Better late than never.
Slow and steady wins the race.
Two heads are better than one.

dialogue.scene: A late arrival at a meeting.

lines.target: Извини, я опоздал на двадцать минут.
lines.english: Sorry, I am twenty minutes late.
lines.translit: Izvini, ya opozdal na dvadtsat' minut.

lines.english: No big deal. It's all for the best.
Really? Why?

replyOptions: Я не знаю, где мой диплом.

lessons.tip: Proverbs are short rhymes everybody knows. Drop them whole into conversation: Время — деньги. Мир тесен. People smile when you do.

lessons.title: Everyday exclamations

items.english: not so fast, it didn't work out that way

sentences.english: Let's go, come what may!

sentences.target: Ты думаешь, он придёт? Как бы не так!
sentences.english: You think he will come? No way!
sentences.translit: Ty dumayesh', on pridyot? Kak by ne tak!

sentences.target: Ни за что не поеду туда зимой.
sentences.english: I will never go there in winter.
sentences.translit: Ni za shto ne poyedu tuda zimoy.

sentences.english: Take an umbrella just in case.

sentences.target: Я хотел спать, но не тут-то было — соседи шумели.
sentences.english: I wanted to sleep, but no such luck, the neighbours were noisy.
sentences.translit: Ya khotel spat', no ne tut-to bylo — sosedi shumeli.

sentences.english: As luck would have it, it started to rain!

fills.english: We at least saw the Kremlin.
Take money just in case.
Fine, so be it, I will help.
If worst comes to worst, we will walk.

dialogue.scene: Bad luck on a trip.

lines.english: We missed the train!
Unbelievable! What do we do?
Maybe we take the bus?

replyOptions: Так и быть, поедем на автобусе.

lessons.tip: Set phrases do not translate word for word: как бы не так means 'no way', not 'how it might not'. Learn when to use them, not the grammar.

lessons.title: Particles

sentences.target: Ты же знаешь, я не люблю спорить.
sentences.english: You know I don't like arguing.
sentences.translit: Ty zhe znayesh', ya ne lyublyu sporit'.

sentences.target: Мы ведь договорились встретиться в пять.
sentences.english: After all, we agreed to meet at five.
sentences.translit: My ved' dogovorilis' vstretit'sya v pyat'.

sentences.target: Вот мой телефон, звони в любое время.
sentences.english: Here is my phone, call any time.
sentences.translit: Vot moy telefon, zvoni v lyuboye vremya.

sentences.english: Well, there it goes, it started to rain!
He doesn't like coffee at all.

sentences.target: Я всё-таки пойду, хотя очень устал.
sentences.english: I will go anyway, even though I am very tired.
sentences.translit: Ya vsyo-taki poydu, khotya ochen' ustal.

fills.english: But you know where he lives.
There, now everything is ready.
'He won't come.' 'Oh, really?'
I just wanted to help.

dialogue.scene: Chatting about weekend plans.

lines.english: Shall we go to the cinema tomorrow?
But I work until seven.

lines.target: Ну и что? Фильм в девять.
lines.english: So what? The film is at nine.
lines.translit: Nu i shto? Fil'm v devyat'.

lessons.tip: Particles (же, ведь, вот, ну) have no direct English: they add tone like 'you know' or 'come on'. Hear them, copy the melody, do not translate.

lessons.title: Ты and вы

sentences.english: Can we switch to 'ty'?

sentences.target: Давай на ты, мы же друзья!
sentences.english: Let's use 'ty', we are friends!
sentences.translit: Davay na ty, my zhe druz'ya!

sentences.target: К директору я обращаюсь по имени-отчеству.
sentences.english: I address the director by name and patronymic.
sentences.translit: K direktoru ya obrashchayus' po imeni-otchestvu.

sentences.english: It is awkward for me to say 'vy' to an old friend.

sentences.target: В письме я пишу вежливо и формально.
sentences.english: In a letter I write politely and formally.
sentences.translit: V pis'me ya pishu vezhlivo i formal'no.

sentences.english: With kids I speak informally.

fills.english: May we use 'ty'?
With a client it is better to speak politely.
He uses 'ty' with everyone and it is overly familiar.
I address him as 'vy'.

dialogue.scene: Meeting a colleague's father.

lines.english: Hello! My name is Sergey Petrovich.
Nice to meet you! I am Alex.

lines.target: Давай на ты, Алекс. Так проще.
lines.english: Let's use 'ty', Alex. It's easier.
lines.translit: Davay na ty, Aleks. Tak proshche.

replyOptions: Я с вами согласен, это дача.

lessons.tip: ты for friends, family, kids; вы for strangers, elders, bosses and groups. To switch, ask: Давай на ты! The older/higher person usually proposes.

lessons.title: Colloquial

items.english: to get hooked, to zone out on
to bother, to go to the trouble

sentences.english: It was like, really funny.
Damn, I forgot my phone at home!
Yesterday's party was great, fun!
This meme is just insane.

sentences.target: Я залипаю в телефоне весь вечер.
sentences.english: I zone out on my phone all evening.
sentences.translit: Ya zalipayu v telefone ves' vecher.

sentences.english: Don't be slow, let's go already!

fills.english: Dude, you look great!
I am too lazy to bother.
This is totally on point!
He got hooked on memes yesterday.

dialogue.scene: Texting a friend after a party.

lines.english: Damn, yesterday was insane!
Yes, the party was great.
How long were you there?

lessons.tip: Colloquial words are for friends only: блин (damn), классно (cool), жесть (crazy bad/good). Fine in a bar, wrong in a formal email.

lessons.title: Reduced speech

items.english: what do you mean, I mean

sentences.english: Hi! How are things?
'Will you come?' 'Yeah, sure.'
'Want tea?' 'Nope, thanks.'
Faster, or we will be late!
Obviously, he knows everything.

sentences.target: Ты в курсе? Завтра созвон в десять.
sentences.english: Are you aware? Tomorrow there's a call at ten.
sentences.translit: Ty v kurse? Zavtra sozvon v desyat'.

fills.english: Come here, or else it will be late.
What do you mean? I don't understand.
Are you aware that he left?
'Are you tired?' 'Sort of.'

dialogue.scene: Quick chat in the corridor.

lines.target: Здрасьте! Ты в курсе, что совещание перенесли?
lines.english: Hi! Do you know the meeting was moved?
lines.translit: Zdras'te! Ty v kurse, shto soveshchaniye perenesli?

lines.english: Nope. To when?
To three o'clock.

lessons.tip: Spoken Russian swallows sounds: здравствуйте → здрасьте, ну ладно → нуладно, не-а = no. Listen for the shorthand, you do not have to produce it.

lessons.title: Sounding local

items.english: long time no see (how many years, winters)

sentences.english: Long time no see! How's life?

sentences.translit: Skol'ko let, skol'ko zim! Shto novovo?

sentences.english: Same old, work and home.
sentences.translit: Da vsyo po-staromu, rabota i dom.

sentences.english: 'How are you?' 'Hanging in there, no complaints.'
Don't disappear, drop by!

sentences.target: Я на связи, пиши в любое время. Пока-пока!
sentences.english: I am reachable, write any time. Bye-bye!
sentences.translit: Ya na svyazi, pishi v lyuboye vremya. Poka-poka!

fills.english: Long time no see!
How's life? What's new?
Don't disappear, write to me!
Same old, no news.

dialogue.scene: Bumping into an old friend on the street.

lines.english: Wow, hi! Long time no see!

lines.target: Сколько лет, сколько зим! Как сам?
lines.english: Long time no see! How are you?
lines.translit: Skol'ko let, skol'ko zim! Kak sam?

lines.target: Да всё по-старому. А у тебя что нового?
lines.english: Same old. And what's new with you?
lines.translit: Da vsyo po-staromu. A u tebya shto novovo?

lessons.tip: Sounding local = the little greeting rituals: Как жизнь? Что нового? Всё по-старому. Say them fast, smile, and move on.
